jp: 新鮮[しんせん]な野菜[やさい]{を|o-object}買[か]う{ために|tameni-purpose}、毎朝[まいあさ]市場[いちば]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: To buy fresh vegetables, I go to the market every morning.
why: A goal you act on directly is plain-form verb plus ために.

jp: 旅行[りょこう]{の|no-possessive}お金[かね]{を|o-object}貯[た]める{ために|tameni-purpose}、外食[がいしょく]{を|o-object}減[へ]らしています。
en: I am cutting back on eating out in order to save money for the trip.
why: A deliberate goal and the action taken for it are linked by ために.

jp: 節約[せつやく]{の|no-possessive}{ために|tameni-purpose}、昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]{は|wa-topic}家[いえ]{から|kara-from}お弁当[べんとう]{を|o-object}持[も]っていきます。
en: To save money, I take a packed lunch from home.
why: With a noun, の plus ために means 'for the sake of'; ように would mean 'like'.

jp: 新[あたら]しい店[みせ]{を|o-object}開[ひら]く{ために|tameni-purpose}、彼[かれ]{は|wa-topic}銀行[ぎんこう]{から|kara-source}お金[かね]{を|o-object}借[か]りました。
en: He borrowed money from the bank in order to open a new shop.
why: His purpose is stated with the verb plus ために.

jp: 友[とも]だち{に|ni-recipient}プレゼント{を|o-object}選[えら]ぶ{ために|tameni-purpose}、デパート{で|de-place}一時間[いちじかん]歩[ある]き回[まわ]りました。
en: To choose a present for my friend, I walked around the department store for an hour.
why: The goal of choosing a gift is expressed by verb plus ために.

jp: 妹[いもうと]{の|no-possessive}{ために|tameni-purpose}、母[はは]{は|wa-topic}誕生日[たんじょうび]{の|no-possessive}ケーキ{を|o-object}焼[や]きました。
en: My mother baked a birthday cake for my little sister.
why: A beneficiary is marked with の plus ために; ように would make it 'like my sister'.
